A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, tables, and figures are readable, including v1's post-reference galleries and v2's supplementary material.

before.justification: v1 reports original vectorization examples and quantitative comparisons on ten images, including runtime, reconstruction error, and vector compactness in Tables 1–2.

after.justification: v2 reports original experiments on 100 images, perceptual and semantic comparisons, and ablations in Section 7 and supplementary Section 9.

M1.justification: v1 jointly optimizes structural and pixel-wise primitives at successive simplification levels using visual, structural, and length losses. v2 instead optimizes structural vectors with an overlap penalty, fits and freezes their colors, then performs separate visual refinement. SDS simplification also changes from reduced guidance with a text prompt to an empty prompt.

E1.justification: v2 explicitly includes emoji-style inputs alongside photos and clipart, modestly extending the reported image variety. v1 already covers flat illustrations and realistic images in Figures 10–11. The vectorization and recoloring tasks remain; the increase from ten to 100 evaluation images primarily changes sample size.

E2.justification: The main comparison expands from LIVE and O&R in v1 to LIVE, O&R, DiffVG, and SGLIVE in v2. Bilateral filtering also joins Gaussian filtering and superpixel simplification in the simplification comparisons.

E3.justification: The principal evaluation changes from ten images at 256 primitives to 100 images with 64, 128, and 256 primitives. v2 adds VGG-based LPIPS and caption-based CLIP evaluation, changes VeC containment from over 90% to over 85%, and caps structural primitives at half the comparison budget.

E4.justification: v1 already compares SDS simplification with Gaussian filtering and superpixels. v2 extends this comparison to reconstructed vector layers and adds controlled tests without the simplification sequence, structural optimization, and overlap loss (Figures 9–10 and supplementary Figures 17–19). These directly examine previously untested component contributions.

E5.justification: v1 Table 2 reports cross-image standard deviations for both MSE and VeC. v2 retains VeC standard deviations in Table 1 but presents MSE curves without dispersion in Figure 12. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 replaces the ten-image numerical comparisons with broader aggregate results and adds LPIPS, CLIP, and ablation findings. Reported mean VeC changes from 43.9% to 73.8%, but the dataset and containment threshold differ, preventing a same-setting performance comparison. v1's per-image runtime results are removed.

T1.justification: Mathematical changes are concentrated in the objective definitions: v1's length-regularized joint objective is replaced by an overlap-regularized structural objective and separate visual fidelity loss in v2. Neither version develops formal theorems or proofs; the rewritten SDS gradient alone does not establish new theory.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains progressive simplification for compact, editable layered vectors. v2 presents two-stage reconstruction and superior semantic alignment as explicit contributions, while removing v1's claim that the optimization avoids local minima.

C2.justification: v2 Section 4.2 explicitly acknowledges shape distortion during ordinary SDS simplification and explains preserving macrostructure through unconditional noise. v1 instead emphasizes increased variation from reduced guidance. v2 also removes the concluding qualification that the method excludes stylization and leaves it to future work.

D1.justification: PyTorch, Adam, learning rates, and hardware disclosures remain. v2's supplement supplies Douglas–Peucker tolerance, filter parameters, and comparator initialization schedules. However, v1's explicit 100/500-iteration vector-optimization schedule and project-homepage link are no longer provided.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially recast around image vectorization and layer decomposition. v2 adds positioning against SAMVG, SuperSVG, SGLIVE, and texture-aware vectorization, alongside extensive layer-decomposition literature. v1's separate vector-generation and sketch-abstraction discussions, including several associated citations, are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and method narrative are extensively rewritten. The method is reorganized around two reconstruction stages, the earlier Results and Experiments organization becomes an integrated Evaluation section, and dedicated supplementary sections organize ablations and implementation details.

P2.justification: v2 redraws the pipeline and introductory illustrations, adds ablation displays and metric curves, restructures tables, and substantially reorganizes the galleries and page layout. Some examples are retained. Supplementary Figures 20–21 have mismatched captions describing simplification filters although their panels compare vectorization methods.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens support for the central claims: comparisons include a relevant segmentation-guided baseline, multiple primitive budgets, perceptual and semantic measures, and controlled component ablations missing from v1. These address important weaknesses of the earlier ten-image evaluation. Runtime evidence and some reproducibility details are lost, and caption errors remain, but the stronger experimental validation provides a clear net improvement. The changed VeC settings do not establish a direct cross-version performance gain.
